Analects.label: sayings_dialogues
Analects.note: Archetypal sayings collection ('zi yue' records) accreted over generations; excavated Zhongni Said / Kongzi Said manuscripts confirm the collection-of-sayings formation process.

Gongsun_Longzi.label: systematic_treatises
Gongsun_Longzi.note: Six extant dialectical essays (lun) on names and actualities from a lost fourteen; the White Horse piece is framed as a debate dialogue but argumentative essay form dominates; some would place it with rhetorical handbooks — medium.

Guanzi.label: anecdote_anthology_compilations
Guanzi.note: Heterogeneous anthology of material from many authors over centuries, compiled/edited by Liu Xiang (76 of 86 chapters survive); mixes essays, verse (Neiye-type) and dialogues — compilation itself is the transmitted form.

Guiguzi.label: rhetoric_persuasion_manuals
Guiguzi.note: Technical manual of persuasion and rhetorical technique (gui/bai, opening/closing, psychological manipulation of interlocutors), distinct from argumentative treatise and anecdote; cf. Conde 2021 (doi:10.17398/1886-9440.15.101).

Han_Feizi.label: systematic_treatises
Han_Feizi.note: 'A selection of essays in the Legalist tradition' (incl. the first Laozi commentaries), but famously rich in anecdotes (Chushuo/Shuolin stores) and contains the persuasion chapter Shuinan; essays dominant — contested.

Huainanzi.label: anecdote_anthology_compilations
Huainanzi.note: 21-essay compiled encyclopedia presented to the Han throne; miscellany-form compendium integrating argument, anecdote, quotation and cosmological system — anthology/compilation.

Kongzi_Jiayu.label: sayings_dialogues
Kongzi_Jiayu.note: 'School Sayings of Confucius': an Analects-type compilation of Confucius sayings, conversations and anecdotes sharing the 'Kongzi said' collection tradition; dominant form is recorded speech.

Laozi.label: verse_aphorisms
Laozi.note: Collection of short rhymed poetic/aphoristic chapters consolidating earlier sayings (Guodian/Mawangdui evidence); the only book in the corpus whose dominant transmitted form is verse.

Liezi.label: anecdote_anthology_compilations
Liezi.note: Eight-chapter compilation of didactic anecdotes, parables and narratives (Liu Xiang redaction; received via Zhang Zhan); anecdote-dominant but with discursive strata — medium.

Liji.label: anecdote_anthology_compilations
Liji.note: Han ritual compendium (L'Haridon): an anthology of heterogeneous ritual records, conversations, narratives and doctrinal chapters (incl. Zhongyong and Daxue) — compilation form.

Liutao.label: sayings_dialogues
Liutao.note: Cast as instruction dictated in dialogue by Tai Gong to Kings Wen and Wu of Zhou (ruler-advisor Q&A frame), yet traditionally classed as a military strategy treatise; mixed — contested.

Lushi_Chunqiu.label: anecdote_anthology_compilations
Lushi_Chunqiu.note: Deliberately structured encyclopedic compilation (ji/lan/lun divisions) integrating argumentative essays with historical anecdotes and quotation; miscellany (zajia) tradition per Heng Du.

Mencius.label: sayings_dialogues
Mencius.note: Conversations with rulers form the basis of the text (dialogue collection), but long sustained argumentative passages (esp. books 3 and 6) approach treatise form; mixed — assigned to dominant dialogue form, hence contested.

Mozi.label: systematic_treatises
Mozi.note: Core is the ten-triad argumentative essays (earliest sustained Chinese treatises), but the received book also contains dialectical canons, anecdotal sections about the master, and technical siege-defense chapters; dominant form is the essay — contested.

Shangjunshu.label: systematic_treatises
Shangjunshu.note: Policy-argumentative essays dominate, but Pines shows a heterogeneous composite text with dialogue-framed chapters and fragmentary aphoristic strata; mixed — contested.

Sima_Fa.label: systematic_treatises
Sima_Fa.note: Terse normative expository prose on military ritual, law and administration (Ban Gu classed it under rites); only 5 of an originally much larger text survive — fragmentary transmission, hence medium.

Sunzi_Bingfa.label: systematic_treatises
Sunzi_Bingfa.note: Thirteen continuous expository chapters each devoted to one aspect of warfare; the archetypal systematic military treatise, no dialogue or anecdote frame.

Wei_Liaozi.label: systematic_treatises
Wei_Liaozi.note: Military-theoretical text: first half theoretical/argumentative chapters, second half terse military-regulation (bingshi) chapters; expository treatise form dominant but internally bipartite — medium.

Wuzi.label: sayings_dialogues
Wuzi.note: Received text is framed as Marquis Wu of Wei asking / Wu Qi answering (ruler-master dialogue), but catalogued among the Seven Military Classics as systematic military doctrine; form (dialogue) vs received characterization (treatise) — contested.

Xiaojing.label: sayings_dialogues
Xiaojing.note: Framed entirely as a Confucius-Zengzi conversation (question-and-answer classic), but transmitted and received as a short doctrinal treatise ('classic treatise'); genuinely mixed form — contested.

Xunzi.label: systematic_treatises
Xunzi.note: Collection of titled argumentative essays (lun-form discussions such as 'Discussion of Heaven', 'Dispelling Obsessions'); the paradigm of the systematic philosophical treatise in the corpus.

Zhongyong.label: systematic_treatises
Zhongyong.note: Transmitted as a discursive doctrinal treatise (traditionally attributed to Zisi; embedded as a Liji chapter), though it opens with a string of 'The Master said' quotations; treatise form dominant.

Zhuangzi.label: anecdote_anthology_compilations
Zhuangzi.note: 'Consists of stories and maxims... many anecdotes, allegories, parables, and fables' — anecdote-dominant, but a multi-stratal anthology (Inner/Outer/Miscellaneous) with dialogue and discursive stretches; mixed — contested.

source_claim: A 5-class partition by dominant transmitted literary form, drawn from genre/form studies of pre-Qin and Han texts rather than from Sima Tan's six schools: (1) verse_aphorisms — rhymed aphoristic verse collections (Laozi as consolidating collected sayings in short poetic chapters; Guodian/Mawangdui accretion evidence, Lebovitz 2021 Early China); (2) sayings_dialogues — Analects-type sayings collections in the 'Kongzi said' yu-lu tradition (Poli & Li 2024 Early China) and ruler-master dialogue records (Mencius, Wuzi, Liutao dialogue frames; Xiaojing as Confucius-Zengzi conversation); (3) systematic_treatises — sustained argumentative/doctrinal essays in lun form and systematic military treatises (Xunzi essays; Mozi triads; Han Feizi essays; Sunzi's 13 continuous expository chapters; Pines 2016 on Book of Lord Shang as policy-essay composite); (4) anecdote_anthology_compilations — anecdote/parable collections and heterogeneous or encyclopedic compilations, incl. the miscellany tradition (Heng Du 2020 JAOS), Han ritual compendium (Liji; L'Haridon 2023), Liu Xiang-edited composites (Guanzi, Liezi), and the Zhuangzi's anecdote/allegory/parable-dominant multi-stratal anthology; (5) rhetoric_persuasion_manuals — technical handbooks of persuasion (Guiguzi; Galvany 2012; Conde 2021; cf. Goldin 2020 on persuasion literature). Class-set grounding: Ning Liu, Genres of Chinese Intellectual Thought (2026); Hanmo Zhang, Authorship and Text-making in Early China (2018). Mixed-form books take their dominant transmitted form and are marked contested. Sealed excavated units (Huangdi_Sijing, Sun_Bin_Bingfa) excluded entirely.
title: Literary-form partition of early Chinese masters literature (confound control)
